PCRMs logo: S1 variants

S1’s looped strand with the transcription factors handled in different ways: where the two pieces of DNA meet, bound along the loop, and between the strands of double-stranded DNA. The mark always sits beside the full PCRMs name. Refer to them by code, e.g. “J6”.

TFs where the DNA meets

J1 One factor

S1 as it is: one key TF where the strand crosses the stem.

J2 Dimer

Two TFs, one on each piece of DNA, binding each other to hold the loop together.

J3 Cluster

Three TFs bridging the two DNA segments, with the key factor in lime.

J4 Mixed shapes

Three different factors at the junction: a circle, a square and a capsule.

J5 Bridge

One elongated factor spanning the gap between the two pieces of DNA.

J6 Ring

A ring encircling both strands, like the cohesin complex that holds real loops closed.

J7 Complex

Several small factors gathered round a central one: a regulatory complex.

TFs along the DNA

A1 Bound along the loop

Factors of different sizes bound along the enhancer loop, plus the key factor at the junction.

A2 Different factors

A square, a capsule and a circle bound along the loop: different TFs at different sites.

A3 Binding sites

Lime marks across the strand where factors bind, clustered on the loop.

A4 Enhancer and promoter

Factors on the loop (enhancer) and one on the stem (promoter).

TFs between the strands

D1 Ladder with TFs

Double-stranded DNA where some base pairs are replaced by bound TFs of different sizes, sitting between the strands.

D2 TFs in the grooves

A double helix with factors of different sizes sitting in its grooves.

D3 Two-tone helix, lime TFs

Two-tone strands with lime factors in the grooves.

P shapes (S1–S9)
